# SETUP

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r load-libraries}
source("setup.R")
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
```

# LOAD DATA

```{r load-water-supplies}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) 
```

```{r load-swi-centroids}
swi_pts <- st_read(here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "swi", "swi_points.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r load-swi-results}
swi_csv <- list.files(
  here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
  pattern    = "swi_exposure.*\\.csv",
  full.names = TRUE
) %>% sort() %>% tail(1)

swi_results <- read_csv(swi_csv)
```

# MAP

Water supply points assigned an SWI exposure value are colored by normalized
SWI migration and connected by a line to the SWI estimation point used to
assign their value. Matched SWI points are colored by their raw Case_C value;
unmatched points are grey. Water supplies more than 50 km from any SWI point
are grey.

```{r build-map}
# Join results onto water supply geometries
ws_mapped <- water_supplies %>%
  inner_join(
    swi_results %>% select(-park_unit, -park_name),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )

ws_exposed <- ws_mapped %>% filter(!is.na(raw_swi_migration))
ws_distant <- ws_mapped %>% filter(is.na(raw_swi_migration))

# Project for nearest-neighbor geometry, then build connector lines
ws_exposed_proj <- st_transform(ws_exposed, 5070)
swi_proj        <- st_transform(swi_pts, 5070)

nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(ws_exposed_proj, swi_proj)
used_idx    <- unique(nearest_idx)
swi_used    <- swi_proj[used_idx, ]  %>% st_transform(4326)
swi_unused  <- swi_proj[-used_idx, ] %>% st_transform(4326)

connector_lines <- st_nearest_points(
  ws_exposed_proj,
  swi_proj[nearest_idx, ],
  pairwise = TRUE
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(4326)

pal <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

mapview(swi_unused,
        col.regions = "grey60",
        color       = "grey60",
        cex         = 3,
        layer.name  = "SWI points (unmatched)") +
  mapview(connector_lines,
          color      = "black",
          lwd        = 1,
          layer.name = "WS → SWI point") +
  mapview(swi_used,
          zcol        = "Case_C",
          col.regions = pal,
          color       = NA,
          cex         = 5,
          pch         = 18,
          layer.name  = "SWI points (matched)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(swi_used) %>%
              select(watershed_id, Case_C)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_exposed,
          zcol        = "norm_swi_migration",
          col.regions = pal,
          layer.name  = "SWI Exposure (norm)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_exposed) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name, raw_swi_migration,
                     norm_swi_migration, rank_swi_migration)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_distant,
          col.regions = "grey60",
          color       = "grey60",
          layer.name  = ">50 km from SWI point",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_distant) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name)
          ))
```

Browsing this map you will probably immediately find some strange examples. 
Using a 50km buffer around a SWI point to limit the search area for assignment
of the exposure value does not consider the possibility that the closest
value may be on an island just off the coast. Forcing water supplies to 
only use SWI points that are in the same polygon as them still does not
resolve the the issue of SWI assignment crossing channels, and runs into the 
issue of no assignment when the closest SWI point is just off the coast, like 
many of the points on the Cape Cod National Seashore.

You will also notice that some water supplies have a `coast_dist_m` value but
no SWI assignment. That means they were within 50 km of the coastline (and so
received a coastal distance) but not within 50 km of any SWI estimation point.

# Decay function weighting (alternative)

Instead of dividing by `coast_dist_m`, this approach multiplies the raw Case_C
value by a linear decay weight: `1 - (coast_dist_m / 50000)`. The weight is
1.0 at the shoreline and 0.0 at the 50 km cutoff (0–1 range, ~5x variation).
Whether this produces meaningfully different rankings than the division approach
depends on whether distance variation or Case_C variation dominates — the chunk
below shows the ranges.

## Range of variation

```{r range-check}
coast_dist_df <- read_csv(
  here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "coast_comp", "coast_distances.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

range_df <- ws_exposed %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, raw_swi_migration) %>%
  mutate(case_c_raw = swi_proj[nearest_idx, ]$Case_C) %>%
  left_join(coast_dist_df %>% select(wsd_source_id, coast_dist_m),
            by = "wsd_source_id")

cat("Case_C (raw SWI migration, meters):\n")
print(summary(range_df$case_c_raw))

cat("\ncoast_dist_m (distance to coast, meters):\n")
print(summary(range_df$coast_dist_m))

cat("\nraw_swi_migration (Case_C / coast_dist_m):\n")
print(summary(range_df$raw_swi_migration))

cat("\nCase_C range ratio (max/min of absolute values):\n")
abs_vals <- abs(range_df$case_c_raw[range_df$case_c_raw > 0])
cat(round(max(abs_vals) / min(abs_vals), 1), "x\n")

cat("\ncoast_dist_m range ratio (max/min):\n")
d <- range_df$coast_dist_m[!is.na(range_df$coast_dist_m) & range_df$coast_dist_m > 0]
cat(round(max(d) / min(d), 1), "x\n")
```

## Build decay-weighted results

```{r build-decay}
# nearest_idx and swi_proj already built in the map chunk
decay_results <- ws_exposed %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name) %>%
  mutate(swi_case_c = swi_proj[nearest_idx, ]$Case_C) %>%
  left_join(coast_dist_df, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    decay_weight       = pmax(0, 1 - (coast_dist_m / 50000)),
    raw_swi_decay      = swi_case_c * decay_weight
  ) %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name, raw_swi_decay) %>%
  add_standardized_indicators("raw_swi_decay", invert = FALSE)

ws_decay        <- water_supplies %>%
  left_join(decay_results, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name"))
ws_decay_exposed <- ws_decay %>% filter(!is.na(raw_swi_decay))
```

## Decay-weighted SWI exposure

```{r map-decay}
mapview(swi_unused,
        col.regions = "grey60",
        color       = "grey60",
        cex         = 3,
        layer.name  = "SWI points (unmatched)") +
  mapview(connector_lines,
          color      = "black",
          lwd        = 1,
          layer.name = "WS → SWI point") +
  mapview(swi_used,
          zcol        = "Case_C",
          col.regions = pal,
          color       = NA,
          cex         = 5,
          pch         = 18,
          layer.name  = "SWI points (matched)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(swi_used) %>%
              select(watershed_id, Case_C)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_decay_exposed,
          zcol        = "norm_swi_decay",
          col.regions = pal,
          layer.name  = "SWI Exposure — decay weight (norm)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_decay_exposed) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                     raw_swi_decay, norm_swi_decay, rank_swi_decay)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_distant,
          col.regions = "grey60",
          color       = "grey60",
          layer.name  = ">50 km from SWI point",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_distant) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name)
          ))
```

## Rank comparison: division vs. decay

Points on the diagonal have identical ranks under both methods. Points above
the line rank higher (higher vulnerability) under decay weighting; points below
rank lower.

```{r rank-comparison}
rank_comparison <- ws_exposed %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_name, rank_swi_migration) %>%
  left_join(
    decay_results %>% select(wsd_source_id, rank_swi_decay),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    range_df %>% select(wsd_source_id, case_c_raw),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )

ggplot(rank_comparison, aes(x = rank_swi_migration, y = rank_swi_decay,
                             color = case_c_raw)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "grey80", high = "red",
                        midpoint = 0, name = "Case_C (m)") +
  labs(
    x = "Rank — division weighting (current)",
    y = "Rank — decay weighting"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
